definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

definitions.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
definitions.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with the constant function.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.
For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, F_tau(f)=(1/6)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, H_tau(f)=(1/3)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv F_tau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Every product is spatial and [G(s)]_0^tau=G(tau)-G(0).

definitions.type: unfiltered time-step map and its iterates
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f). For positive integer L set tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau. Define u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L. There is no spatial cutoff in this recurrence.
For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For tau>0, t_n=n*tau and k!=0, hat(R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3))(k)= -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Output at k=0 is zero. Initially this formula is on Fourier polynomials; bounded extension is proved below. Terms with a zero input frequency vanish since one phase is zero.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t) P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].
For I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, Cint_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t) P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt; time-independent inputs are read as constant paths.

For tau>0, nonnegative integer n, t_n=n*tau and t in [t_n,t_n+tau], Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)= (1/2) integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,f)ds, initially for a time-independent smooth mean-zero f; the endpoint normal form below gives its L2 extension.

For smooth mean-zero step data f at t_n=n*tau, write F_n(t)=Stage_(n,tau)(t;f), z_n=f+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_n+tau)+R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f), V_n(t)=f+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, Y_n=V_n-z_n, rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. For f=S_(-t_n)u^n, concatenate V_n as V and the increments rho_n as Rres, with Rres(0)=0. Continuity of V at grid points is a proved property, not an assumption.

definitions.type: normalized periodic KdV equation and exact-solution convention
definitions.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

inputs.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution u of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x, obtained by smooth approximation, and sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions on [0,T]. For two real mean-zero L2 data q,r of norms summing to at most B0, the exact solutions satisfy sup_[0,T]||u_q-u_r||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-r||_2. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves all Sobolev norms and for smooth data v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Consequently M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the datum ball.

S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality and zero mean. On mean-zero inputs, uniformly in real t: ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infty<=C||f||_2; ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-23/14))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For every A0 in H^1, ||A0||_infty<=C||A0||_(H^1). For A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Also ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, ||A0||_(H^(-23/14))<=||Dinv A0||_2 for mean-zero A0, and ||J_t(A0,B0)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||B0||_2 whenever the right side is defined. For smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Moreover J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Cint_I(f,g,h). These identities hold stepwise for piecewise smooth paths, and Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]_(s=n*tau)^t/6.

binders.type: periodic function or mean-zero distribution as stated

inputs.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there are C>0,tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero datum u0 of H^gamma norm <=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the fixed scheme and its Interp path satisfy sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C*tau^gamma, hence max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Constants are independent of every higher Sobolev norm and of spectral support.

output.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

locals.declaration: Define u0_m=P_(<=m)u0 for positive integers m.
Take the unique solution with datum u0 supplied by N001.
Fix arbitrary positive integer L in the asserted timestep range.
Define tau=T/L for the chosen L.

locals.type: sequence of exact smooth solution paths
locals.declaration: Take u_m to be the unique exact solution for each u0_m supplied by N001.

argument.text: H001-H003 give the ranges T>0, 0<gamma<=1, R>0. Fix arbitrary real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma and assume L1: ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Let u0_m=P_(<=m)u0. The data are real mean-zero Fourier polynomials, ||u0_m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and ||u0_m-u0||_2 tends to zero by the convergent Fourier norm sum. N001 supplies exact solutions u_m,u with a common M bound and sup_[0,T]||u_m-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0_m-u0||_2 tending to zero. The solution u has precisely the continuous distributional smooth-approximation convention in the target.

produces.statement: The real mean-zero polynomial approximants u0_m have H^gamma norm <=R and their exact solutions converge uniformly in time in L2 to the specified u.

argument.text: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2. Indeed N005 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 product bound; consequently F_tau:L2->H^1 is a continuous quadratic map. The first term of H_tau is a product of inverse derivatives. Its second has the continuous bilinear scalar mean P0(f^2) multiplied by S_tau Dinv f. Its third is the H^1 product (S_s Dinv f)^3 followed by Dinv. Its fourth is the product of D^(-2)F_tau(f) and Dinv f, with unitary S factors and a final D^(-2). Each is continuous into L2; all scalar coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for this fixed tau. Hence the map and all of its finitely many iterates are continuous. The same formulas preserve reality and zero mean: explicit P, outer inverse derivatives, and the zero-mean factor in the scalar-mean term show this directly.

produces.statement: For every fixed theta>0 and finite nonnegative msteps, Psi_theta and each of its first msteps iterates are continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2 and preserve reality and zero mean.

argument.text: Take C,tau0 from N011, determined only by T,gamma,R. Fix an arbitrary positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Applying N011 to u0_m gives the same error bound C*tau^gamma for every m. By F002 the numerical iterates converge in L2 at each of the finitely many grid points, and F001 gives uniform convergence of the exact solutions. The reverse triangle inequality, followed by the maximum over L+1 points, passes the estimate to u0. Since C and tau0 depend only on T,gamma,R, their choice is uniform over the entire datum ball and all L, this is the full conclusion P, including n=0. The finite-step continuity argument uses fixed tau only and imposes no support restriction or numerical H^gamma bound. Discharge L1 into the stated datum-ball antecedent and universally quantify u0 and the allowed L.
